key_insight: Medical Heuristic Learning uses an LLM-guided, non-gradient workflow to turn clinical tabular data into interpretable, auditable Python decision rules instead of opaque model weights.
clinical_relevance: The approach is designed for clinical decision support where transparency, robustness to small and imbalanced datasets, and adaptability to changing features matter.
method: LLM-guided statistical probes and medical knowledge probes
Rule synthesis followed by code-level iterative refinement
Versioned pure-Python decision rules for deterministic execution
evidence_signal: Across medical datasets, the method matched state-of-the-art performance while showing strong results in small-sample and highly imbalanced settings and helping reduce catastrophic forgetting under feature evolution.
watch_item: Because the system relies on hand-updated rule logic and evolving feature definitions, deployment will require careful validation, maintenance, and clinical oversight.
paper_title: Medical Heuristic Learning: An LLM-Driven Framework for Interpretable and Auditable Clinical Decision Rules
